docs.title: LOF-P-006: Versioning
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Each release carries a version IRI and version number, and every earlier release remains resolvable.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Legal analysis is often retrospective. Users must be able to retrieve exactly the version of an ontology that was in force when data was annotated.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. Each release declares owl:versionIRI of the form https://w3id.org/lof/{id}/releases/{version}/{id}.owl and owl:versionInfo.
  2. Version numbers follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). A MAJOR increment signals a change that can alter inferences over existing data.
  3. Each release is tagged v{version} in the repository, and the change is recorded in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: make release VERSION=x.y.z sets both annotations. Then tag and push.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: https://w3id.org/lof/odp-001/releases/0.1.0/odp-001.owl

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
The version IRI resolves to the tagged file, and the changelog describes the release.

Automated check: Version IRI resolution is tested during review.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-006-versioning.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-007: Textual definitions
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Every class and relation has a precise, non-circular textual definition.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: In law, the meaning of a term is often the point in dispute. Definitions make the intended meaning checkable by lawyers and domain experts who will never read an axiom.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. Every class and relation in the ontology's namespace has exactly one English definition, recorded with skos:definition or IAO:0000115.
  2. Class definitions take genus and differentia form where possible: "An X is a Y that Z", where Y is the asserted parent.
  3. Definitions do not use the term being defined, and cite a source (statute, case, treatise) with dcterms:source where one exists.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Add the definition when the term is created. Protégé's annotation panel supports both properties.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: legal role: "A role that inheres in a person or organization in virtue of recognition by a legal institution and that is realized in legally significant processes." (Illustrative only.)

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Definitions are present, match the asserted parent, and are intelligible to a legal expert.

Automated check: SPARQL check missing-definition-violation.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-007-definitions.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-008: Clearly delineated scope
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The ontology has a stated scope and a set of competency questions.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Scope statements prevent overlap between member ontologies and let users decide quickly whether an ontology fits their needs. Competency questions make scope testable.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. The ontology header has a dcterms:description, and the README contains a scope statement saying what the ontology covers and excludes.
  2. The README lists competency questions: questions a knowledge base using the ontology should be able to answer.
  3. The registry entry's domain field agrees with the scope statement.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Write the scope statement and competency questions before modeling begins. They are required in the new ontology request.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: "Covers the conferral, holding, and revocation of legal roles by institutions. Excludes the content of the obligations attached to those roles."

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Scope and competency questions exist and are specific enough to judge overlap with other member ontologies.

Automated check: ROBOT report check missing_ontology_description.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-008-scope.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-009: Orthogonality
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Member ontologies do not duplicate one another's content.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Two classes for the same legal entity, minted in two ontologies, force every user to reconcile them. Orthogonality means each kind of entity is defined once, by the group best placed to maintain it.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. Before minting a term, developers check the registry for an existing member-ontology term with the same meaning.
  2. Where one exists, it is imported or referenced by IRI rather than redefined.
  3. Overlaps found in review are resolved by the maintainers concerned, with the Editorial Working Group mediating.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Import the relevant module from the other member ontology through the catalog, as the template does for BFO.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: An ontology of court procedure reuses legal role from a roles ontology rather than defining its own judge role parent class.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
The reviewer searches accepted ontologies for labels and definitions overlapping the candidate's terms.

Automated check: None yet. A cross-registry label overlap report is planned.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-009-orthogonality.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-010: Jurisdictional transparency
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Classes specific to a legal system or jurisdiction are marked as such and are not presented as universal.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Legal categories vary across systems. A class that silently generalizes from one jurisdiction ("consideration" in common-law contract, say) misrepresents others and produces false inferences when data from several systems is combined.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. The registry entry lists the jurisdictions or legal traditions in scope (jurisdictions), or general if the ontology claims generality.
  2. Classes restricted to particular jurisdictions carry a dcterms:coverage annotation naming them.
  3. Claims of cross-jurisdictional generality are supported by documentation.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Use jurisdiction identifiers in the form ISO 3166 country codes or named traditions (for example, common-law, civil-law), and be consistent within the ontology.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: A class consideration annotated with dcterms:coverage "common-law".

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Jurisdiction-specific classes are annotated. The ontology's generality claims are plausible given its sources.

Automated check: None. Manual review.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-010-jurisdiction.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-011: Logical well-formedness
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Each release is logically consistent and contains no unsatisfiable classes.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: An inconsistent ontology entails everything, and an unsatisfiable class can have no instances. Either defect makes automated reasoning over legal data worthless.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. The ontology, merged with its imports, is consistent under an OWL 2 DL reasoner (HermiT, or ELK for large EL ontologies).
  2. No named class is unsatisfiable.
  3. The check passes before every release.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: make test runs the HermiT check through ROBOT. CI runs it on every push and pull request.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: See the LOF ontology template.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
CI is green on the release commit.

Automated check: robot reason in CI.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-011-consistency.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-012: Naming conventions
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Labels are unique, singular, and follow a consistent lexical style.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Consistent labels make ontologies readable together and reduce errors when terms are chosen from pick lists.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. Every entity has exactly one rdfs:label per language.
  2. Labels are singular nouns or noun phrases, in lower case except for proper nouns and established acronyms.
  3. Labels are unique within the ontology, and preferably within the Foundry.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Use skos:altLabel for synonyms and jurisdiction-specific alternative names rather than adding a second label.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: "legal obligation", not "Legal Obligations"; "European Court of Human Rights" keeps its capitals.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Label style is consistent, and warnings from the label-case check are justified.

Automated check: SPARQL checks missing-label-violation, multiple-labels-violation, and the label-uppercase-warning report; ROBOT report check duplicate_label.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-012-naming.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-013: Documentation
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The ontology has a public repository with documentation and an issue tracker.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Documentation is how users outside the development team learn what an ontology is for and how to use it correctly.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. The ontology has a public repository in, or linked from, the Foundry GitHub organization.
  2. The README states the scope, competency questions, grounding decisions (LOF-P-004), maintainers, license, and how to cite.
  3. Issues can be reported through a public tracker.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The ontology repository template includes a README with these sections and a term-request issue form.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: See the LOF ontology template.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
All README sections are filled in.

Automated check: Registry schema validation of repository and tracker.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-013-documentation.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-014: Responsiveness and maintenance
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Maintainers respond to issues and keep the ontology aligned with its dependencies.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Legal ontologies must track changes in law and in the ontologies they import. An unmaintained ontology gradually becomes wrong.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. Maintainers respond to new issues within 30 days.
  2. The ontology is updated to the current release of BFO and of any member ontology it imports within a reasonable period of their release.
  3. An ontology whose maintainers cannot continue is marked orphaned in the registry, and the coordinators seek new maintainers.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Watch the repositories of imported ontologies, and schedule periodic make imports refreshes.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: See the LOF ontology template.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Issue response history and the date of the last import refresh.

Automated check: None yet. Issue-activity metrics are planned.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-014-maintenance.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-015: Alignment with existing legal standards
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The ontology documents its relationship to established legal information standards.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Legal information already circulates in established formats. Documented mappings let Foundry ontologies annotate that data rather than compete with it.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. Where a relevant standard exists (for example Akoma Ntoso, LegalRuleML, LKIF, ELI, ECLI), the README states whether and how the ontology maps to it.
  2. Term-level mappings, where provided, use skos:exactMatch, skos:closeMatch, skos:broadMatch, or skos:narrowMatch, or a SSSOM mapping file.
  3. Mappings are not asserted as logical equivalences unless the ontological commitments have been checked.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Keep mappings in a separate SSSOM file under src/mappings/ when they are numerous.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: A class for judgments mapped to the Akoma Ntoso judgment document type with skos:closeMatch.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Relevant standards are identified, and mappings use the appropriate SKOS strength.

Automated check: None. Manual review.

docs.title: Feedback and discussion
docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-015-standards.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-016: Documented use
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The ontology has documented users, or a credible plan for use.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Ontologies built for no one tend to drift from real needs. Documented use shows that the ontology solves an actual problem and gives maintainers a community to consult.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. By the time of admission to accepted, the registry entry lists at least one independent use in its usages field (a dataset, application, project, or publication).
  2. At draft and candidate status, a planned use suffices.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Record usages in the ontology's registry metadata file.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: See the LOF ontology template.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Listed usages exist and are independent of the maintainers where possible.

Automated check: Registry schema validation of usages.

docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-016-users.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-017: Locus of authority
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Each ontology has a single named point of contact responsible for it.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Users and the Foundry need to know who can answer questions and make decisions about an ontology.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. The registry entry names one contact person with a working email address and GitHub handle.
  2. The contact person is a maintainer of the ontology, or can reach one promptly.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Set the contact field in the registry metadata. Update it when responsibility changes.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: See the LOF ontology template.

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
The contact is reachable.

Automated check: Registry schema validation of contact.

docs.text: Propose changes to this principle by pull request against docs/principles/lof-p-017-authority.md, or open a thread in Discussions.

docs.title: LOF-P-018: Attribution
docs.text:
Draft for ratification

Part of the founding draft of the LOF principles.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Contributors to the ontology are credited, and it can be cited.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Ontology development is scholarly work. Credit sustains contributions, and citability lets that work count in the academic and professional record.

docs.title: Recommendations and requirements
docs.text:
1. The ontology header lists creators with dcterms:creator and contributors with dcterms:contributor, using ORCID IRIs where available.
  2. Term-level contributions may be recorded with dcterms:contributor on the term.
  3. The README gives a preferred citation.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: Add ORCID IRIs to the header when onboarding each new contributor.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Annotation(dcterms:creator <https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000>)

docs.title: Criteria for review
docs.text:
Creators are listed, and a citation is given.

Automated check: None. Manual review.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
Ontologies and design patterns registered with the Foundry. Status values are defined in the metadata policy. Machine-readable versions: ontologies.yml, ontologies.jsonld.

ID Title Prefix Jurisdictions Status Activity odp-001 LOF-ODP-001: Legal Act and Legal Document ODP001 general draft active odp-002 LOF-ODP-002: Legal Role Conferral ODP002 general draft active odp-003 LOF-ODP-003: Correlative Deontic Positions ODP003 general draft active odp-004 LOF-ODP-004: Minimum Legal Chain ODP004 general draft active

To register an ontology, follow the new ontology request SOP.

docs.title: SOP: New ontology request
docs.text:
1. Check the registry. Make sure no existing ontology already covers the scope (LOF-P-009).
  2. Open a request. Use the New ontology request issue form in the website repository. You will be asked for a title, requested prefix, scope statement, competency questions, jurisdictions, planned use, and contact.
  3. Scope discussion. An Editorial Working Group member responds, usually within 30 days, checking for overlap and agreeing the prefix.
  4. Register at draft status. Once scope and prefix are agreed, open a pull request adding ontology/{id}.md with status: draft. A coordinator merges it. The prefix is now reserved, and the w3id.org/lof redirects are regenerated.
  5. Create the repository. Create lof-{id} in the Foundry organization (or link your own), and initialize it from the ontology template with ./init.sh.
  6. Develop. Follow the principles. Keep CI green.
  7. Request review. When ready, follow the review SOP.

docs.title: SOP: Release
docs.text:
In the ontology repository:

  1. Make sure CI is green on main.
  2. Update CHANGELOG.md with the new version and date.
  3. From src/ontology/, run make release VERSION=x.y.z. This regenerates lof-{id}.owl and lof-{id}-base.owl at the repository root, with version IRI and version info set.
  4. Commit the release files and changelog: git commit -am "Release x.y.z".
  5. Tag and push: git tag vx.y.z && git push && git push --tags.
  6. Optionally, create a GitHub release from the tag.
  7. Check that https://w3id.org/lof/{id}/releases/x.y.z/{id}.owl resolves.

Use semantic versioning (LOF-P-006): PATCH for corrections to labels and definitions, MINOR for new terms, MAJOR for changes that can alter inferences over existing data.

docs.title: SOP: Ontology review
docs.text:
Review moves an ontology from candidate to accepted.

  1. Submit. The contact person opens a pull request changing the ontology's status to candidate, linking a tagged release.
  2. Assign reviewers. The Editorial Working Group assigns two reviewers: one Operations Committee member and one reviewer who is not a maintainer of the ontology.
  3. Review. Each reviewer opens an Ontology review issue using the form, which lists every principle as a checkbox, and records findings for each unmet principle. Automated check results are taken from the ontology's CI.
  4. Revise. Maintainers address findings and tag a new release. Reviewers update their issues.
  5. Decide. When both reviewers recommend acceptance, the change to status: accepted is approved as a substantive change (see Governance), and the review field records the date and issue.

docs.title: Re-review
docs.text: Accepted ontologies are re-reviewed if a principle is amended in a way that affects them, or if an overlap dispute is raised.

docs.title: SOP: Term requests
docs.text:
Anyone may request a new term, or a change to an existing term, in any member ontology.

  1. Open an issue in the ontology's tracker (https://w3id.org/lof/{id}/tracker) using the New term request form. Give a proposed label, definition, parent class, source, and an example of use.
  2. A maintainer responds within 30 days (LOF-P-014), either adding the term, pointing to an existing term, or explaining why it is out of scope.
  3. If the term belongs in a different member ontology, the maintainer transfers the issue there.
